items.title: Wildlife rebounds on Isle of Wight farmland, with bird numbers nearly tripling
items.author: WORLD DESK
items.description: Wildlife recovery has been observed on the Isle of Wight after five years of rewilding efforts. Bird populations at Wilder Little Duxmore nearly tripled, indicating a significant resurgence. Meanwhile, butterfly counts at Wilder Nunwell increased by 117% and bumblebee abundance rose by 64%. Improvements in soil and water quality were also noted, showing the effectiveness of rewilding processes. This recovery highlights nature's potential when given the opportunity to regenerate naturally.

items.title: Drought’s bitter harvest of debt
items.description: As El Niño conditions deepen Telangana’s agricultural distress, failed kharif crops have left farmers saddled with mounting debts, wiped-out investments and little means of recovery. With loan repayments looming and rural livelihoods under threat, Abhinay Deshpande reports on the human toll of the crisis, the growing desperation among farming families and the gaps in support, as experts warn that worsening water scarcity could prolong the distress well beyond this season

items.title: After snake enters daughter's room, Florida couple's stormwater case revived
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: A Florida couple, William and Ashley Merryman, reported significant damage to their home and health risks. After filing a lawsuit, they sought a preliminary injunction against state agencies linked to environmental changes. The district court initially denied their request, citing delayed action and potential financial remedies. However, the appeals court found faults in the lower court's reasoning and has remanded the case for reconsideration.

items.title: 54 rescued sea turtle hatchlings released after first California nests recorded
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: In a historic first for Southern California, two olive ridley sea turtle nests were discovered in September 2026. Due to an imminent tropical storm, the eggs were carefully relocated and monitored at the Aquarium of the Pacific. On November 14, 54 hatchlings emerged and were released into the ocean, followed by another 21 from a second nest on Huntington Beach the next day.

items.title: Psychology says parents sharing fears may make children feel more loved: Study
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: Discussing personal fears can significantly deepen the emotional connection between parents and children, as evidenced by a study revealing that children felt more cherished during these heartfelt dialogues. Exploring sad and anxious emotions creates stronger bonds, allowing parents to share relatable memories. However, it's essential to conduct additional research to grasp the lasting impact of these vital conversations.

items.title: Piramal Pharma raises FY27 growth guidance; analysts see 15-23% upside
items.description: Piramal Pharma is experiencing growth momentum as the CDMO business gains traction and expands its late-stage pipeline. It recently upgraded its revenue growth guidance for FY27 to 19-20%. The recent performance reflects a 28% revenue increase and a 72% rise in Ebitda year-on-year. Investments in complex manufacturing are also improving its capabilities in high-value businesses. Analysts remain optimistic, maintaining a 'Buy' rating on the stock.

items.title: Sebi may examine Tata Steel-APL Apollo deal amid investor concerns
items.description: Tata Steel plans to acquire a controlling stake in APL Apollo Tubes while selling its steel-related businesses. Stakeholders have raised concerns about the deal's governance and its potential impact on minority shareholders. APL Apollo's largest institutional investors have expressed their discontent regarding the structure and debt implications. The arrangement involves multiple transactions affecting ownership and business structure within APL Apollo.

items.title: 'Hard to believe': Ex-India cricketer questions Siraj's continued omission
items.author: PRANAV SHUKLA
items.description: Mohammed Kaif has voiced his astonishment at Mohammed Siraj's exclusion from India's Test team. Siraj, who excelled as the leading wicket-taker during the World Test Championship, has been left out for the second Test. Captain Shubman Gill mentioned that performance was key to their selection choices, while bowling coach Morne Morkel suggested focusing on improvements. This decision continues to stir debate as the two-match series unfolds.

items.title: Big, fat Bihar wedding makes global headlines
items.author: FARYAL RUMI
items.description: Mokama MLA Anant Singh's daughter Shivangi's wedding attracted attention due to its enormous scale and extravagant displays. Over 400,000 guests were invited, with six helipads and a massive feast prepared by 500 cooks. However, food distribution led to chaos as guests struggled to find plates amidst the crowd. Animal welfare concerns arose from the event, particularly regarding horse racing and a captive elephant.

items.title: India playing leading role in global war on terror, says Amit Shah
items.author: TNN
items.description: Amit Shah, the Union home minister, reaffirmed India's unwavering dedication to fighting terrorism while honoring the memories of those affected by the 26/11 attacks. He praised the bravery of both soldiers and innocent civilians, asserting that the Modi government’s unwavering stance against terrorism is garnering global recognition. Shah also highlighted that united action is essential, as terrorism remains a grave threat to humanity.

items.title: Colombo Security Conclave reaffirms commitment to promote regional peace
items.author: TNN
items.description: The Maldives hosted the 8th NSA-level meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave, uniting member states in their shared goal of enhancing regional peace and security. By emphasizing capacity-building and collaboration, the attendees laid out a roadmap for security cooperation through 2026-27, marking a commitment to address evolving challenges. India reaffirmed its resolve to engage actively with CSC countries to foster stronger ties and collective security measures.

items.title: Mumbai police issue lookout circulars against CJP’s Dipke, Ranka, Das
items.author: ABHINAV GARG AND AHMED ALI
items.description: CJP co-convener Saurav Das was barred from flying to London due to a lookout circular. The Centre informed the Delhi high court that this action was taken at Mumbai police's request. Saurav Das's passport is under scrutiny for several discrepancies regarding his identity. His legal team argued that the travel ban infringes upon his fundamental rights. The court proceedings continue as he prepares to respond to the notice issued.

items.title: Ohio lawyer denied partnership wins $2m discrimination award after 9-year suit
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: In a landmark ruling, Pamela Pantages, a lawyer from Ohio, has triumphed in her discrimination lawsuit against her previous employer. The Eighth District Court of Appeals upheld a $2 million jury award, affirming her allegations of being denied partnership due to age and gender bias, as noted in the firm's owner’s comments. This decision corroborates the jury's findings of sex discrimination and contract breaches at The Becker Law Firm.

items.title: Father-son team in South Africa sets 408mph record with 3D-printed drone
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: On December 11, 2025, Mike and Luke Bell shattered records by piloting their Peregreen V4 quadcopter to an astonishing average speed of 408.60 mph, making it the fastest battery-powered quadcopter in history. This remarkable achievement resulted from their dedication to innovative design and rigorous testing, employing advanced aerodynamics and cutting-edge 3D printing techniques. It is a monumental step forward in the realm of drone racing.

items.title: Odisha women turn banana waste into 21,000 festival boats and extra income
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: Odisha's vibrant Boita Bandana festival will witness a creative surge as local women weave miniature boats from banana stems. Supported by around 40 to 50 Self-Help Group members, this innovative project offers a new income stream for the artisans and nearby banana farmers alike. items.title: 28 ancient Gallic coins found with skull fragments, bronze wagon wheel in France
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: Archaeologists exploring Bure in northeastern France uncovered 28 ancient Gallic coins alongside human skull fragments. The site is believed to be a Late Iron Age sanctuary used by the Leuci. In addition to the coins, a miniature bronze wagon wheel was also found, suggesting ritual significance. The discovery contributes to understanding the cultural and religious practices of ancient Gaul. Ongoing studies aim to clarify the site's history and purpose.

items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: This year, London welcomes a spectacular 21-metre Norwegian spruce named Jolly Cheery for its Christmas display. Selected through public voting, this tree represents the enduring friendship between Norway and the UK. To minimize environmental impact, it will be transported in an eco-friendly manner and adorned with energy-efficient lights, set to be unveiled on December 3. Post-Christmas, it will be composted, promoting sustainability.

Instead, he emphasizes the growing necessity for emotional intelligence and insight as cornerstones of true intelligence. Huang predicts that our ability to foresee and address complex, unspoken challenges will be pivotal in defining the intelligence of tomorrow.

items.author: TNN

The ruling addresses the competence of administrative members in handling questions of law and conflicting judgments. The judgment is applicable prospectively and does not allow reopening of past decisions.

items.author: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY

Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu criticized the justification threshold for such a change, ultimately mandating that Anand Mohan must surrender within a month.

items.title: 23 coins stolen from 1712 Dutch shipwreck return to Australia after global probe
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: After extensive efforts, Australia has reclaimed twenty-three silver coins from the infamous Zuytdorp shipwreck, which was lost at sea in 1712. The recovery operations spanned both the Netherlands and the United States, revealing a surge in illicit interest since 2019. In light of this, Australian authorities ramped up their monitoring, culminating in local resident Ashley Patterson's guilty plea for breaching underwater heritage laws linked to these invaluable artifacts.

items.title: Pension, insurance for 15 lakh gig workers likely by year-end
items.author: SHIVA RAJORA
items.description: The government plans to announce a pension scheme and health insurance for gig workers soon. Workers enrolled on the e-Shram portal will be the primary beneficiaries of these initiatives. The National Social Security Board will discuss contributory models, including a 2% turnover-based contribution from platforms. Trade unions have suggested immediate health and accident cover for these workers during onboarding.

items.author: TNN
items.description: In a move reflecting ongoing tensions, the Indian Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has urged Netflix to limit access to Pakistani content, particularly an upcoming series set to debut on December 4. Netflix has not clarified the series' availability in India, as industry groups pursue legal actions against Pakistani media.

items.title: Supreme Court sets timer for FSSAI, companies to implement warning labels
items.author: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY
items.description: The Supreme Court has instructed the FSSAI to implement front-of-package labeling within four months. Companies will have one year to comply with these regulations after the notification. Labels will indicate high levels of sugar, saturated fat, and salt inside red hexagonal shapes to protect consumer health. The court emphasized the importance of preventing public health crises associated with unhealthy food consumption.

items.title: US techie likely behind dozens of Mumbai bomb threats held in Tamil Nadu
items.author: MATEEN HAFEEZ
items.description: Sharath Subramanian Shankar, a 28-year-old techie from Tamil Nadu, is implicated in sending over 1,500 hoax emails. These emails warned of attacks on significant locations in Mumbai, including the BMC office and the Bombay Stock Exchange. He was detained by Tamil Nadu police after returning from the US based on intelligence from Mumbai police. Another suspect, Ankit Shankhwar, is being investigated for supplying fake email accounts used in these threats.
